note:
Ann Baily B Brown, a widow living on her own means, with a housekeeper and two servants at 13 Park Terrace (#378) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the four was in the record, and 13 Park Terrace held only 1921, so 1891 is free.

**The directory gives her name a fuller form.** Wright's Directory prints 'Mrs. A. Baily-Browne' at 13 Park Terrace in 1894-95 - hyphenated and with a final e, against the census's Brown. The name is entered as the census has it, since that is what the return says and an import does not rename anybody; the directory spelling is recorded here so the two can be recognised as one woman. She had gone by 1898-99, when number 13 belongs to P. W. Allen, solicitor.

13 Park Terrace is a census-only property in the record, which is to say it is known from returns rather than from a building description. Its later life is consistent: Frederick Dunnill in 1913-14, Miss Margaret Gill in 1915-16, and Alice Margaret Gill with Ada Causer on the 1921 return. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 13 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613); 1898-99, page 115 (id 165291).
